unit: Unit 12: Everyday Life with Your Computer
title: Which shop is real?
drDigitalIntro:
Fake shops copy a real one closely enough to fool a quick glance.
• The giveaway is almost always the web address, not the page design. Anyone can copy a design.
• Look for a misspelled name, an odd ending, or http:// where you expected https://.
• A price that is far below everyone else is the second-best clue.
• One of the three shops below is not what it claims. Find it.

playgroundTask.instructions: One of these three shops is fake. Click the one you should not trust.

items.label: Shop
items.preview: https://shop.example — Kettle, $24.99 — free returns within 30 days

items.label: Sh0p Deals
items.preview: http://sh0p-deals.xyz — Kettle, $4.99 — PAY NOW, no returns

items.label: Book Shop
items.preview: https://bookshop.example — Paperbacks from $6.50 — delivery in 3 days

playgroundTask.fakeExplanation: Three things gave it away at once: a zero instead of an 'o' in 'sh0p', an address ending in .xyz rather than the shop's own name, and http:// instead of https://. The impossible price and 'no returns' confirm it.

drDigitalSuccess: You read the address rather than the page. That is the habit that keeps money where it belongs.
drDigitalHint: Ignore how the pages look. Read the three web addresses and find the one that is pretending.
